segments.source: Start with the brewer you use most. Intelligentsia Decaf Black Cat gives a specific espresso dose and output. Organic Decaf House gives a filter ratio. Stumptown explicitly discusses both espresso and drip. Counter Culture publishes several brew methods and its changing blend history. Equator gives unusually detailed current component origins and several filter recipes. A nominally versatile bag cannot make one grind setting work for espresso and drip.

segments.source: The US FDA says an eight-fluid-ounce cup of brewed decaf typically contains 2–15 mg caffeine. That range is useful context, but cannot be applied as a measurement of a specific coffee, espresso shot or serving. Swiss Water itself says residual caffeine in a brewed cup varies with dose and method. Buyers who need exact exposure should seek product-specific information and professional advice for their own situation.

segments.source: Intelligentsia recommends 18 g coffee to 45 g finished espresso for Decaf Black Cat. That 1:2.5 ratio is a useful start if your basket can hold the dose. It is not a promise that a shot takes a particular number of seconds on your grinder. Its Organic Decaf House page instead recommends 1 g coffee to 18 g water for drip or pour-over. For a 20 g filter dose, that arithmetic gives 360 g water. Do not copy the filter ratio into a portafilter.
